subject.title: TUI /sessions list: gateway-injected inbound metadata block used as session title (shows 'untrusted metadata' for all sessions)

question: Should maintainers salvage the existing conflicting fork PR or close it and authorize a narrow replacement fix for this issue?
rationale: The issue is valid, but an open non-maintainer PR with closing syntax already owns the exact bug and is conflicting/not maintainer-editable, so automation should not race it without a maintainer branch-path choice.

options.title: Authorize a narrow replacement
options.body: Close or supersede the conflicting fork PR after opening a maintainer-editable replacement that covers current sync, async, and agent-tool paths.

options.title: Ask the fork author to rebase
options.body: Keep this issue paired to the existing fork PR and wait for the author to resolve conflicts and update proof.

options.title: Adopt the fork manually
options.body: A maintainer can manually cherry-pick the useful diff into an OpenClaw branch because maintainers cannot push to the fork PR.

recommendation.title: Authorize a narrow replacement
recommendation.body: Close or supersede the conflicting fork PR after opening a maintainer-editable replacement that covers current sync, async, and agent-tool paths.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has adjacent ownership signals for session origin metadata and session picker/display hygiene, and is the best routing candidate among the source-history owners.
